rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should test a balanced multimodal configuration with strong encoders (pca_n2000 for RNA and imagenet_vit_l for images) and weighted fusion, which are common effective choices. This clarifies the baseline performance of a well-rounded multimodal setup and reduces uncertainty about encoder and fusion choices.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, weighted fusion) achieves 0.5318 accuracy. This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt (a more sophisticated model) while keeping other components identical. This clarifies whether RNA encoder choice significantly impacts performance, a critical design decision. It balances exploration of key components with logical extension of previous findings.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (imagenet_vit_l image encoder) achieves higher accuracy than config_025 (resnet50 image encoder). This experiment tests whether switching to resnet50 with the same pca_n2000 RNA encoder and weighted fusion could improve performance, clarifying the impact of image encoder choice. It balances exploitation (building on config_001's RNA encoder) and exploration (testing resnet50) while maintaining singleprofile setting.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (pca_n2000 RNA + imagenet_vit_l image) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests scvi_n200 RNA encoder with the same image encoder and fusion method, clarifying if RNA encoder choice significantly impacts performance. It balances exploitation (building on current best) and exploration (testing a new RNA encoder).

Existing evidence shows that config_038 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l with weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.5375). This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders but with avgpool aggregation, which could improve performance by better handling multiprofile data. It balances exploitation of strong components (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l) with exploration of aggregation methods, addressing uncertainty about how aggregation impacts results.

The existing evidence shows config_047 (multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA, ImageNet ViT-L, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.706). This experiment tests transformer aggregation and concat fusion (config_048) to explore if alternative aggregation/fusion strategies could further improve performance. It directly addresses uncertainty about optimal multimodal integration methods for multiprofile data, leveraging the strong multiprofile signal while exploring critical design choices.

Existing evidence shows config_047 (multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.706). This experiment tests transformer aggregation with the same RNA/image encoders but different aggregation method, which could improve performance. It clarifies whether transformer aggregation (vs avgpool) enhances results for this promising configuration, balancing exploitation of current strengths with exploration of aggregation methods.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_009) achieve high accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders but with transformer aggregation and concat fusion (vs. weighted fusion in config_009), clarifying if fusion method impacts performance. It balances exploitation of promising components with exploration of design choices critical to accuracy.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile setups with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_009: 0.724989) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests a similar configuration but with pca_n2000 RNA encoder instead of scvi_n200, which could clarify if encoder choice impacts performance. It balances exploitation of proven aggregation/fusion strategies with exploration of RNA encoder variations, maximizing the chance to find the optimal configuration within the remaining budget.

The existing evidence shows that configurations with multiprofile settings and transformer aggregation (e.g., config_009: 0.724989) perform best. This experiment tests replacing the image encoder (resnet50 vs. imagenet_vit_l) in config_009, a critical design choice with uncertain impact. It clarifies whether the image encoder choice affects performance in this high-performing setup, potentially identifying a superior configuration.
